sections.title: Vision of the Locusts
observations: In this vision, Amos sees a swarm of locusts devouring the crops of Israel, symbolizing impending judgment. The locusts represent God's judgment on the nation for their sins, particularly their social injustices and idolatry.
Amos intercedes for Israel, pleading with God to spare them. This highlights the role of the prophet as an intercessor, showing God's mercy even in the face of judgment.

sections.title: Vision of the Fire
observations: The second vision depicts a great fire consuming the land, representing another form of divine judgment. This fire symbolizes the destruction that will come upon Israel due to their unfaithfulness.
Again, Amos intercedes, and God relents, demonstrating His willingness to listen to the pleas of His prophet.

sections.title: Vision of the Plumb Line
observations: In the third vision, God shows Amos a plumb line, indicating that He is measuring Israel against His standard of righteousness. This signifies that Israel has fallen short and will face consequences for their actions.
The plumb line represents God's unchanging standard of holiness, and the vision serves as a warning that judgment is imminent.

sections.title: Amaziah's Opposition
observations: Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, opposes Amos and accuses him of conspiracy against the king. This reflects the tension between true prophetic voices and institutional religion that often seeks to maintain the status quo.
Amos responds by affirming his calling from God, emphasizing that he is not a professional prophet but a shepherd called to deliver God's message.

importantVerses.commentary: Amos' plea for mercy shows the heart of a true prophet who desires the restoration of his people rather than their destruction.
The plumb line symbolizes God's standard of righteousness, reminding us that God measures His people against His holiness.

questions: What does the imagery of the locusts and fire reveal about God's judgment and mercy?
How does Amos' role as an intercessor inform our understanding of prayer and advocacy for others?
What does the plumb line signify in terms of God's expectations for His people today?
How do we respond to opposition when we stand for God's truth, as Amos did?
